notes: Acoustic metadata is sourced from the Vedic Śikṣā corpus (phonetics Vedāṅga). IPA transcriptions follow standard Sanskrit phonology per Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā. Articulation positions follow Taittirīya Prātiśākhya sthāna classification.

ध.vedic_pitch: anudātta (low tone) — associated with sustaining, grounding
ध.mantra_frequency_note: Associated with the sustaining vibration; Ṛgveda Prātiśākhya classifies dha as having a nāda quality of dhāraṇa (support).

क.vedic_pitch: udātta (high tone) — associated with creative action
क.mantra_frequency_note: Ka is the bīja of creation (Brahmā); Taittirīya Prātiśākhya notes ka as the first of the kaṇṭhya sparśa consonants.

रं.vedic_pitch: udātta — associated with the rising flame; fire = upward movement
रं.mantra_frequency_note: Raṃ is the Agni-bīja; the anusvāra (ṃ) represents the resonant hum of fire. Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā groups ra with the antaḥsthas.

अ.mantra_frequency_note: A is the first of the three phonemes of Auṃ (A-U-M). Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad identifies A with the waking state (jāgrat). All consonants are said to rest on A.

ॐ.sthana: tri-sthāna (throat + palate + lips with nasal resonance)
ॐ.vedic_pitch: tri-svara (all three tones unified) — the complete sonic form of Brahman
ॐ.mantra_frequency_note: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad devotes its entire 12 verses to Om. Taittirīya Upaniṣad 1.8 calls it the brahma-vacana. The anusvāra is the turīya (fourth, transcendent) element.

हं.mantra_frequency_note: Haṃ is the bīja of ākāśa (space element) and also of prāṇa. For Koshas it represents the subtlety of the sheaths. Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā classifies ha as the lightest of consonants.

लँ.mantra_frequency_note: Laṁ is the pṛthivī-bīja (earth element seed), associated with Mūlādhāra chakra and the physical world (bhūrloka). The l phoneme represents lateral spreading — apt for loka (world, spread).

हँ.mantra_frequency_note: Haṁ is the ākāśa-bīja — space is the subtlest element, and ha being the lightest consonant (keval prāṇa/breath) represents empty space. Viśuddha chakra bīja.

गुं.vedic_pitch: udātta — rising, ascending — the guru lifts the student
गुं.mantra_frequency_note: Guṃ is the Gaṇapati-related bīja; also the Guru-bīja in many traditions. Ga represents the movement/going (gam) associated with the Guru who leads the student from darkness (gu) to light (ru).

क्रीं.prayatna: compound: plosive + semivowel + long vowel + anusvāra
क्रीं.vedic_pitch: ūrdhva (ascending) — Kāla = time which ascends and transforms
क्रीं.mantra_frequency_note: Krīṃ is the bīja of Kālī, the Goddess of time. The compound ka+ra+ī+ṃ represents: creation (ka) + fire (ra) + consciousness (ī) + resonance (ṃ). Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā discusses compound bījas in the context of maṅgala-vācaka.

ह्रीं.prayatna: compound: fricative + semivowel + long vowel + anusvāra
ह्रीं.vedic_pitch: mādhya (middle tone) — Māyā operates at the middle level between absolute and manifest
ह्रीं.mantra_frequency_note: Hrīṃ is the Māyā-bīja and the Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja. Ha (space) + Ra (fire) + Ī (power) + Ṃ (resonance) = the creative illusion that sustains the manifest world. Shared by Śakti, Mokṣa in their creative/liberating aspects.

यं.mantra_frequency_note: Yaṃ is the vāyu-bīja (air/wind element), the element of prāṇa. Anāhata chakra bīja. Ya represents movement (yā = to go) — prāṇa is the moving vital force. Also Yoga bīja (union through breath).

ऋ.vedic_pitch: svarita — the cosmic resonance tone; Ṛgveda itself is named from this vowel
ऋ.mantra_frequency_note: Ṛ is unique in Sanskrit — a vocalic retroflex. The Ṛgveda's name derives from ṛc (hymn) + veda. Ṛ represents the cosmic resonance of truth (ṛta). Taittirīya Prātiśākhya gives ṛ special status as the svara of ṛṣis.

सं.vedic_pitch: svarita — balanced; saṃ = together, perfectly formed
सं.mantra_frequency_note: Saṃ is the prefix-bīja of completeness and perfection. The prefix saṃ appears in saṃskāra (perfectly made), saṃskṛta (perfectly constructed language), saṃnyāsa (perfect renunciation). Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā classifies sa as the lightest of the ūṣman group.

ऐं.sthana: tālu (palate) — seat of knowledge and discrimination
ऐं.vedic_pitch: udātta — the highest tone; wisdom resonates at the highest frequency
ऐं.mantra_frequency_note: Aiṃ is the Sarasvatī-bīja — the Goddess of knowledge, speech, and learning. The compound a+i+ṃ = existence (a) + wisdom (i) + resonance (ṃ). Pāṇinīya-Śikṣā discusses sandhi-svaras (compound vowels) including ai.

so'ham.vedic_pitch: svarita — the union of cosmic (sa) and individual (aham) consciousness
so'ham.mantra_frequency_note: So'haṃ ("I am That") is the Puruṣa-bīja and the natural mantra of every breath: So (inhalation) + Haṃ (exhalation). 21,600 repetitions per day with normal breathing — Śiva Sūtra.

chakra_pancha.varna_class: pañca-mahābhūta bīja sequence (five element seed syllables)
chakra_pancha.mantra_frequency_note: The six chakra bījas form the complete spectrum of manifest consciousness from earth to pure awareness. Taittirīya Prātiśākhya maps each to its elemental articulation region.

yajna_om.prayatna: praṇava compound + svāhā (svā = well + hā = offerings)
yajna_om.vedic_pitch: all three tones — yajña encompasses the full tonal spectrum
yajna_om.mantra_frequency_note: Svāhā is the ritual offering bīja used in Agni-yajña. Every oblation to the fire is preceded by Om and concluded with Svāhā. Taittirīya Saṃhitā treats Svāhā as an avyaya (indeclinable) like Om.

moksha_hrim.prayatna: compound: fricative + semivowel + long vowel + anusvāra
moksha_hrim.vedic_pitch: ūrdhva (ascending) — liberation is the highest ascent
moksha_hrim.mantra_frequency_note: In Śākta tradition, Hrīṃ is also the Mokṣa-bīja — Ha (space/liberation) + Ra (fire/purification) + Ī (consciousness/śakti) + Ṃ (resonance) = the path to liberation.

yoga_yam.mantra_frequency_note: Yaṃ for Yoga reinforces the vāyu-bīja connection — yoga is fundamentally the joining (yuj) through prāṇāyāma (breath control). Same bīja as Prāṇa but applied to the context of union.

prakrti_hrim.prayatna: compound: fricative + semivowel + long vowel + anusvāra
prakrti_hrim.vedic_pitch: mādhya (middle tone) — Prakṛti operates at the manifest level
prakrti_hrim.mantra_frequency_note: Hrīṃ as Prakṛti-bīja represents the creative matrix of nature. Sāṃkhya identifies Prakṛti with the three guṇas; the compound hrīṃ embodies their interplay.

shakti_hrim.vedic_pitch: tri-svara — the triple power of Śakti
shakti_hrim.mantra_frequency_note: Śakti is represented by the tri-bīja Hrīṃ (Māyā-śakti) + Klīṃ (Kāma-śakti/attraction) + Aiṃ (Jñāna-śakti/knowledge). The Durgā Saptaśatī uses these three as the primary Śākta bījas.
